{{Short description|Estonian chemist}}

[[File:Olev Träss.jpg|thumb|Olev Träss]]
'''Olev Träss''' (born 1931 in [[Tartu]]) is an [[Estonia]]n chemist who lives in Canada. He is a promoter of Estonian community in Canada.<ref name="err.ee">{{cite web |title=Eesti lugu. Olev Träss – eesti teadlane {{!}} Vikerraadio |url=https://vikerraadio.err.ee/814999/eesti-lugu-olev-trass-eesti-teadlane |website=ERR |access-date=7 May 2021 |language=et |date=21 October 2017}}</ref>

He has graduated from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="err.ee" /> He joined the [[University of Toronto]]'s Department of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry in 1958, was made full professor within about a decade, and retired in 1995. At present he is listed as Professor Emeritus. <ref name="media.utoronto.ca">{{cite web | title=Olev Trass|url=https://media.utoronto.ca/bluebook/olev-trass/|website=media.utoronto.ca|access-date=14 August 2026|language=en}}</ref>

He is one of the founders of Tartu Institute ([[:et:Tartu Instituut|:et]]) in Toronto, and also its president. He is also one of the founder of Kotkajärv Forest University ([[:et:Kotkajärve|:et]]).<ref name="err.ee" />

In 2007 he was awarded with [[Order of the White Star]], IV class.<ref name="president.ee">{{cite web |title=Teenetemärkide kavalerid: Olev Träss |url=https://www.president.ee/et/vabariik/teenetemargid/kavaler/5356/olev-trass |website=www.president.ee |access-date=5 May 2021}}</ref>

In 2021 he received Aino Järvesoo prize for his contribution to sustaining and developing Estonian culture and language abroad.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aino Järvesoo auhind {{!}} Pere Sihtkapital|url=https://peresihtkapital.ee/aino-jarvesoo-auhind/|access-date=}}</ref>
